input_evidence: Guest booted to the standalone demo; the org.blauos.consoleshell job (PID 5) ran an interactive /bin/sh on /dev/console; its '# ' prompt appears on the serial log.
Typed command line 'echo LIVE_INPUT_MARK_A7' + CR (inject-01): the shell executed it; the output line LIVE_INPUT_MARK_A7 appears in the serial log after the tty echo of the command.

Ctrl-C while 'cat' was the foreground process (inject-02/03): NOT effective. The byte was consumed by the line discipline (echoctl printed ^C; it is not inserted as data), but cat kept running and the following typed lines (echo AFTER_CTRL_C_OK, export TERM=ansi, vim ..., the insert text, :wq) were swallowed by cat's stdin and appear twice in the log (tty echo + cat copying stdin to stdout). Interpretation: the interrupt character reaches the line discipline, but no SIGINT is delivered to the foreground process - consistent with the console session having no established foreground process group for signal delivery. SIGINT delivery is a genuine remaining gap, not a documentation error.
Ctrl-D EOF (inject-11): effective. cat exited on EOF and the shell prompt '# ' returned.
Because cat was still foreground, the vim session in run 1 never started; vim evidence is from run 2.
shutdown_evidence: Guest serial: 'PDArmPlatformExpert: host requested stop; sending SIGTERM to PID 1' (power-button patch polling PL061 0x20060000 irq 37 pin 6, announced at boot line 133).

launchd: 'Userspace shutdown begun' -> consoleshell (PID 5) was still running; launchd waited its 20-second exit timeout, logged 'Exit timeout elapsed (20 seconds). Killing', then 'Userspace shutdown finished' (~20 seconds).
Kernel: reboot(RB_HALT), vfs_unmountall, 'CPU halted', 'PDArmPlatformExpert: QEMU PSCI HVC SYSTEM_OFF'.
Host: public guestDidStop callback 20 seconds after requestStop; probe exit 0; no orderly-shutdown-timeout, no force-stop-recovery.

input_evidence: Sanity 'echo RUN2_SHELL_OK' executed; output line present.

Ctrl-C alone at the shell prompt (inject-02): echoed as ^C and consumed by the line discipline; the next command 'echo AFTER_PROMPT_CTRL_C' executed uncorrupted (output line present). At an idle prompt this is indistinguishable from a normal line-abort; run 1 shows the same byte does not interrupt a foreground child.

Full-screen vim over the console (TERM=ansi, builtin termcap): vim started (E1187 'Failed to source defaults.vim' - expected, the tiny toolkit vim ships no runtime files), drew a full 24-line screen (ESC[H ESC[2J, 22 tilde lines, status line '" /tmp/live-vim-edit-2.txt" [New File]'), accepted insert-mode text ('i' + sentence + CR), accepted ESC then ':wq' (2.5 s gap to exceed ttimeoutlen), and reported '2 lines, 60 bytes written'.
Verification: 'cat /tmp/live-vim-edit-2.txt' printed the exact inserted sentence 'Second run: full-screen vim over the VirtualBuddy console.' as shell-command output.

Ctrl-D EOF at the shell prompt (inject-10): the interactive shell exited; the serial log ends at '# ^D' and the later shutdown shows only mDNSResponder as a remaining job (consoleshell already gone), confirming EOF terminated the shell.
shutdown_evidence: Same guest chain as run 1: 'host requested stop; sending SIGTERM to PID 1', launchd userspace shutdown (0 seconds this time - no lingering console shell), reboot(RB_HALT), unmounts, PSCI SYSTEM_OFF.
Host: guestDidStop 1 second after requestStop; probe exit 0.

sigint_fix_run_3.mechanism: Root cause of the run-1 Ctrl-C gap: launchd opens job descriptors with O_NOCTTY before setsid() (launchd core.c job_setup_fd), so the consoleshell's session never acquired /dev/console as controlling terminal; the console tty's t_pgrp stayed NULL and tty_pgsignal delivered VINTR's SIGINT to no process group. The kernel line discipline was already correct. Fix: getty/login-style userspace binding - vm/console_login.c (built by scripts/vm/build_console_login.py into usr/libexec/blauos-console-login, sha256 c1a2226c875e93fb81c1dd472ff60786a3efeaa595c8707efdc35ef411c7dbe5, libSystem-only) opens /dev/console without O_NOCTTY, issues TIOCSCTTY and tcsetpgrp, then execs /bin/sh -i as a login shell. vm/org.blauos.consoleshell.plist now runs the launcher (job sha256 3c8e70bc9af588e165f4ea73deafc9d50eb93482346df3ea65b2e3343a0750b0).

serial_shows: console-login succeeded (no BLAUOS_CONSOLE_LOGIN fail line anywhere; shell prompt present)

foreground 'cat' + Ctrl-C: '^C' echoed, the shell prompt '# ' returned immediately, and the next typed command 'echo CAT_INTERRUPTED_OK' executed with output - SIGINT now reaches the foreground process (contrast run 1: cat kept swallowing input until EOF)

vim insert mode + Ctrl-C: vim left insert mode (its SIGINT handler); the following ':wq' executed as a normal-mode command and wrote exactly the inserted sentence ('2 lines, 56 bytes written'); 'cat /tmp/run3-vim.txt' printed 'Run three: SIGINT reaches the console foreground pgrp.' with no stray bytes
Ctrl-D EOF exited the shell ('# ^D' at end of session)
